sections.title: The Hidden Math: RDH Clinical Production vs. Janitorial Labor
sections.content: Across Nassau County, Suffolk County, and Queens, NY, Registered Dental Hygienists (RDHs) command $52 to $68+ per hour in base wages (plus payroll taxes and benefits), and produce $180 to $300+ per hour in clinical hygiene revenue. Certified Dental Assistants (CDAs) earn $24 to $34+ per hour. When a practice owner or office manager asks clinical staff to stay 30–45 minutes late every evening to vacuum waiting rooms, mop operatory floors, empty trash, and scrub patient restrooms, the practice isn't "saving money" — it is paying surgical-grade hourly wages (often at 1.5x overtime rates) for unverified janitorial work.

sections.title: 5 Reasons In-House Staff Cleaning Hurts Your Dental Practice
sections.content: Dentist-owners and dental office managers who transition from staff-cleaned offices to XIRI's managed nightly terminal cleaning report immediate improvements across five operational metrics:
items: 1. Hygienist & Assistant Retention — In post-exit surveys across private dental practices, being forced to scrub toilets and mop floors after 8 hours of clinical patient care is consistently cited as a top grievance driving RDHs and assistants to competing practices or DSOs
2. Rushed End-of-Day Disinfection — At 5:30 PM, exhausted clinical staff want to go home. Floors get spot-mopped, restroom corners get skipped, and EPA List N wet contact times are cut short

3. Lost Chair Time & Overtime Creep — Paying 3 clinical team members 30 minutes of daily overtime at $45–$90/hr (loaded overtime rate) costs $1,350 to $2,700+ per month — more than a dedicated nightly professional terminal cleaning crew

4. Cross-Contamination Between Restrooms & Operatories — Without a dedicated 4-color microfiber system and commerciallaundering protocol, staff frequently use the same mop bucket across patient restrooms, reception, and clinical hallways

5. Office Manager Supply Burnout — Instead of focusing on treatment plan presentation, insurance aging, and recall schedules, your Dental Office Manager wastes hours ordering paper towels, soap cartridges, and trash liners
